title: fix(guard): a later refusal at a rung must void its older cached verdict, so the lane re-runs
description:
## the defect

`getAllCachedPassedReviews` keeps every `passed` given at the hash, and `getOneCacheSafePeerReviewArtifact` then serves the latest of those. a LATER given at the same rung that refused (`constraint`) or malfunctioned is filtered out of the cache, so the guard serves the OLDER passed verdict and holds the lane: it never re-runs.

the judge reads the latest given per slug, finds the refusal, and scores it 1 blocker (`asPeerGivenVerdict`, unreadable). the stance tool refuses a stance on it ("there is no verdict to take a stance on"). so neither a stance nor a re-run can clear the residual, and a depth-0 arrive changes naught.

## the repro (measured)

- an l3 lane (`rhx enroll claude ...`) gives a real verdict at hash H, iteration i9
- a driver at clone depth 1 re-arrives; the lane refuses with `clone enroll depth budget spent`, given i10 at the same hash H
- a human arrives from depth 0: the lane is held on the i9 verdict, no i11 is written, and the judge still counts the i10 refusal as 1 blocker

## the cure

a passed given is cache-eligible only while it is its rung's latest given at the hash:

```js
const getAllCachedPassedReviews = (input) => input.reviews.filter((r) => r.exitClass === 'passed' &&
    !isSupersededAtRung({ review: r, reviews: input.reviews }));
const isSupersededAtRung = (input) => input.reviews.some((other) => other.index === input.review.index &&
    other.iteration > input.review.iteration &&
    other.exitClass !== 'passed');
```

a refusal BEFORE a pass voids naught; a refusal at another rung voids naught at this one.

## the clamp

a red-then-green clamp exists downstream as `prove.guard-reruns-a-lane-whose-latest-given-refused` (uladkasach/dev-env-setup), applied there as a local pnpm patch on 0.42.1. arms:

- [i9 passed, i10 constraint] → miss
- [i9 passed, i10 malfunction] → miss
- [i9 passed] → i9
- [i9 constraint, i10 passed] → i10
- a refusal at another rung → this rung's i9 kept

## also owed

the guard reads a refusal with no counts as a terminal constraint (0 blockers), while the judge scores the same given as 1 blocker. the two readers should agree on one verdict for one file.
